summary: F1: Suspicious sign-ins from a Cloudvault VPS in Germany outside account baseline (8 events). F2: Most sign-ins originate from Germany (8 events), corroborating the anomalous geography. F3: VPN appliance vpn-edge-01 runs firmware listed in CISA KEV with multiple CVEs, exposing an external access path. Gate verdict: escalate at 0.51 confidence; exposed asset touchpoint with partial signal chain and no confirmed abuse.

risk.rationale: Verified evidence shows suspicious sign-ins from a non-baseline VPS ASN (F1, CONFIRMED 0.52, T1078.004) with most sign-ins from DE (F2, LIKELY 0.5), plus a VPN appliance (vpn-edge-01, firmware 22.7R2.3) running a product with multiple CISA KEV vulnerabilities (F3, CONFIRMED 0.49, T1133/T1190). However, there is no confirmed account takeover chain (no credential change, MFA registration, inbox rule, or lateral movement observed), F2 is only LIKELY not CONFIRMED, and a data-quality conflict (DQ vpn_session_order failing) undermines session ordering for the VPN appliance. This matches the escalate criteria: active exposure (KEV-listed edge appliance) combined with conflicting/insufficient evidence requiring human judgment to determine whether the VPN vuln enabled the suspicious sign-ins or whether the sign-ins are unrelated.
